title: Projection compatibility of the first graph constituent
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring, f:X→Y a morphism of arbitrary schemes, c a supplied open/proper compactification and t=(a,e,p) a proper/open/proper presentation of f. Form the concrete graph presentations t1,t2 and comparison factors B1,B2,D of [def-sf-graph-projection-stages]. For every M in D(X_et,A) and K in D(Y_et,A), tensor B1_M with K and then apply the successive word projection of the first graph presentation t1. The result equals the compactification projection followed by B1 evaluated at M tensor Lf*K. These are the exact sfGraphWordProjection coefficient compositors [def-sf-etale-graph-word-projection]. No other graph constituent is used in this assertion, and no qc, Noetherianity or boundedness is required.

proof.text: Use the proved section_tensor helper in SfEtaleGraphTransferTensor to obtain monoidality of the canonical pullback section comparison. The proved derived_star_id_conjugate helper in SfExactExchangePasting identifies the canonical identity direct-image comparison with the conjugate of the exact identity pullback comparison; transport it to left-derived pullback. Composition of conjugates identifies the graph insertion eta with the conjugate of the section comparison. Apply the categorical conjugate/projection equation and the successive projection formula for a composite adjunction. This gives the tensor square for inserting Rs followed by Rq, without inverting a projection map.

Use the proved properStrength_comp helper and mixed_twisted_projection helper of CompactificationProjectionComposition for the direct-image compositor Rp Rc to Rr and the Cartesian square with q,b,c.i,p. Paste these squares with the insertion square by naturality of the outer proper projection, the open projection, the exchange, and the compositor. The private graph_tensor_paste proves this pasting directly in arbitrary categories.

Identify the coefficient path. Expand the square pullback comparison as an inverse compositor followed by a compositor. Apply leftDerivedUpperStarComp_assoc'_app to s,b,p and to s,q,c.i; cancel the s,q compositor and use the left identity law. Move the outer pullback compositor through the s,b comparison by naturality, then apply map_leftDerivedUpperStarComp_hom_app_leftDerivedUpperStarComp_inv_app to (s b),p,c.g. The result is exactly the two inverse compositors defining the coefficient of sfGraphWordProjection.

Move coefficient maps through the open and proper projection maps using naturality in the right argument. Postcompose the pasted tensor square with the compactification coefficient comparison. The coefficient identity of the previous step gives sfGraphWordProjection on the left. Naturality of sfGraphFirstSideIso gives sfCompactProjection on the right. Expand the endpoint wrappers, including sfGraphProjectionWord, and normalize composition to obtain the unchanged theorem.
